eyebrow: Python for Data Science · Chapter 3, Lesson 15
subtitle: ORDER BY, RANK(), and GROUP BY ... COUNT(*) — the pandas versions.

code:
orders.sort_values("amount")
# smallest (45.00) first; missing amount lands LAST

orders.sort_values("amount", ascending=False).head(3)
caption: Ascending is the default; pandas puts missing values at the end either direction, unless you say otherwise.

code:
orders.sort_values(["status", "amount"],
                    ascending=[True, False])

# like ORDER BY status ASC, amount DESC
# .reset_index(drop=True) for a fresh 0,1,2 index
caption: Each column gets its own direction. Sorting reorders rows but doesn't renumber the index.
Both skip missing values — a direct "give me the top 3" without a full sort.

code:
orders["rank"] = orders["amount"].rank(ascending=False)

# order 4 (310.00) -> rank 1.0
# order 5 (missing) -> rank NaN
caption: rank is pandas' RANK() — ranks come back as floats because tied averages can produce halves.
Probably the most-typed method in exploratory analysis — sorted most to least common.

eyebrow: Proportions, missing values, and a flat table
code:
orders["status"].value_counts(normalize=True)
# shipped 0.625  (62.5%)

# dropna=False counts missing too
# .reset_index() turns it into a 2-column table
caption: normalize=True gives proportions instead of counts. Column names from reset_index vary by pandas version.
